summary: Full-stack testing of Freshly Grocery MVP. Backend: 33/34 pytest passed (1 skipped - ASAP outside window, 1 failed - brute-force lockout). Frontend storefront and admin dashboard load cleanly, admin login works, all 11 admin pages render without errors, cart drawer works, add-to-cart requires auth as expected. UI checkout could not complete via automation because IST-time-of-run put all slots as past leadtime and ASAP outside operating hours (a legitimate timing constraint, not a bug in the flow itself — API-level checkout tested successfully via pytest).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout is INEFFECTIVE behind ingress/proxy. Lockout identifier is 'request.client.host + email', but request.client.host is the immediate proxy pod IP (e.g., 10.208.135.194 / 10.208.135.198) which rotates per request across ingress replicas. Repeated wrong logins (tested 6+) all return 401 and never 429. Attackers can brute-force freely. Fix: use X-Forwarded-For first hop (or lock by email only, or by email + X-Real-IP).

integration_issues.flow: Checkout slot selection when browser TZ differs from IST
integration_issues.issue: Checkout page requests slots for 'today' derived from browser local date (UTC in test env). Backend computes availability in Asia/Kolkata. When IST rolls into the next day (~00:00-02:30 IST) but the browser is still in the previous UTC date, the checkout shows 'No slots available today. Try ASAP delivery if offered.' while ASAP may also be disabled (outside 09:00-21:00 IST). Recommendation: compute the checkout 'today' using Asia/Kolkata timezone so it matches the backend's slot computation, and/or allow user to pick a next-day slot when today has none.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout identifier to properly identify the client behind the ingress proxy (use X-Forwarded-For or lock by email). Currently the security control is a no-op in this environment.
In frontend Checkout.js, compute the 'today' date string using the Asia/Kolkata timezone (not the browser local timezone) so requested slots align with backend's IST-based availability.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: login_attempts identifier = ip:email using request.client.host works only when the app is exposed directly. Behind an ingress, this must trust X-Forwarded-For. Also consider locking per-account (email only) with capped total attempts.
orders.py: _reserve_inventory rolls back on failure but is not truly atomic (no MongoDB transaction). Concurrent stock races are possible. For MVP acceptable, but note.

coupons.py validate_coupon: start_date/end_date comparisons use datetime.now().isoformat() (naive) vs stored ISO strings — timezone mismatch may cause coupons to appear active/expired incorrectly at UTC boundaries.
delivery.py compute_slots: max_orders_per_slot check runs count_documents per slot — N+1 query pattern, fine for small volumes but should be aggregated.
products.py enrich uses N+1 inventory queries in list endpoints — for larger catalogs consider $lookup or batched fetch.
wishlist.py get_wishlist: discount_percent duplicates logic already in products.enrich — extract shared helper.
payments.py webhook: does not update order status even when signature is valid — appears incomplete (only returns ok).

settings.py: no admin_settings_toggle protection against removing keys; PUT filters None values but should probably persist explicit false too (Optional[bool]=None conflates 'unset' vs 'set to false' — currently works only because pydantic defaults are None).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all pages load, admin flow OK; checkout completion untested via UI due to IST window)

Only known failure: test_brute_force_lockout — will pass only after main agent fixes the client-IP identification behind the proxy.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout key = f'{ip}:{email}' where ip = request.client.host. FastAPI/Starlette gives request.client.host = the peer of the TCP connection, which behind Kubernetes ingress is the ingress pod IP (varies across replicas per request). Therefore each of the 5+ failed attempts writes a fresh login_attempts document keyed to a different pod IP, and the count never reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 for any single identifier. Repro: POST /api/auth/login with the same wrong email 7 times; observe backend logs — client host alternates and status is 401 every time. Mitigation: (a) trust the X-Forwarded-For header's leftmost IP (with ProxyHeadersMiddleware) or (b) use only the email as the identifier (with an IP-based secondary limiter) or (c) add a global rate-limiter middleware like slowapi keyed by X-Real-IP.
